title: Trace of a Tape Transfer
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $x$ be an input word, let $S$ be a symbol alphabet, and let $w$ be a finite word over $S$. Choose distinct work tapes $s$ and $d$, and let $c$ be a configuration in the sweep phase. Suppose that, for every integer $p$ with $-1\le p\le |w|$, tape $s$ at position $	ext{head}_s(c)+p$ contains exactly the symbol or blank specified by storing $w$ from offset $p$ (with positions outside the word blank). Then the run of the transfer machine from $c$ follows this trace: during the forward pass, both selected heads advance by one at each step and the destination tape is filled with the corresponding symbols of $w$; during the return pass, both heads move back across the word while the source cells are erased; and after the passes the machine remains in the done phase. The trace configurations use the prescribed copied tape contents and head positions, and its final configuration has the done phase and the tape contents at the start of the return pass.
hypotheses_covered: Natural number k, input word x, symbol alphabet S, and finite word w
Distinct source and destination work-tape indices
Initial configuration d is in the sweep phase
For every integer p between -1 and the length of w inclusive, source tape content at the corresponding offset equals the stored-word content
caveat: The formal statement equates the run with a piecewise trace built from private configuration constructions; the prose describes those constructions but cannot fully expose their exact cell-by-cell definitions concisely.
